profile.name: Carlotta
profile.introduction: Carlotta, the second daughter of the esteemed Montelli family, embodies innate nobility and a refined appreciation for art. Her elegance is matched by her unconventional spirit, unshackled by tradition. To ensure her family’s future, she alternates between dual roles, addressing delicate "troubles" behind the scenes.
profile.review:
Carlotta is a 5-star Glacio Pistol DPS who has a large portion of her damage window gated behind her Ultimate. She was the first ever character to possess 2 different Ultimates, she uniquely can cast up to 6 different attacks each counted as an Ultimate, and she is still one of the most ranged damage dealers in the game, making her great at avoiding enemy attacks. Carlotta is a character who is defined by her rotation consistency and her ease of use, following a traditional playstyle of building up a Forte gauge to unleash the biggest portion of her damage.

Key Mechanics & Rotation Concepts

Like many older characters, Carlotta is a fundamentally simple character to understand. She wants to build up Substance, her first Forte gauge, through Skills and Intros. This allows her to cast a special Heavy Attack that consumes this Forte gauge, which she can then follow with her Ultimate. After casting it, she has access to 4 special ranged attacks called Death Knells that, when cast, follow into her final Ultimate, ending her rotation.

Other than this, Carlotta will inflict a debuff called Deconstruction which allows her to ignore 18% of enemy DEF using all of the most relevant attacks in her rotation. She can also stun enemies for 1.5s upon hitting them with her first Skill. She may only use her enhanced Forte Heavy Attack every 22s, and her Ultimate once every 25s. Those represent almost all of her damage (aside from her Skills that also have a 14s cooldown), so overall she is very cooldown-gated when it comes to her key abilities.

Finally, provided Carlotta has cast her Forte Heavy Attack before her Ultimate, she gains an 80% buff to all damage multipliers in her Ultimate window, that expires upon switching her out. It is hence heavily disincentivized to switch her out once her Ultimate has been cast. Her Outro is a simple burst of damage like several older DPS Outros, nothing special there. Her most noteworthy mechanic is her ability to cast 6 different attacks counted as Ultimates (her 4 Death Knells and her 2 Ultimates), which has been used for temporary endgame buffs when she was still recently released, however this mechanic has not been utilized for a while at this point.

Meta Position & Conclusion

Carlotta is one of the simplest characters to understand meta-wise in the game. She has two main routes for her premium teams: Zhezhi + Shorekeeper, her on-release team or Lynae + Mornye, the recent universal buffing core released in version 3.0. While in theory, Lynae Mornye is Carlotta’s best team, they are so high-value for modern damage dealers with a higher ceiling than Carlotta that most players still stick to a Zhezhi Shorekeeper team if they have access to it. And for the players who don’t… Carlotta’s performance becomes undeniably subpar.

While it’s true that on her release, Carlotta w as the uncontested best DPS in the game, in the modern era we currently are a part of, she only really sees use in the side towers of ToA, or in Endstate Matrix. Her lack of significant, constant AoE damage makes her a really bad pick for Whimpering Wastes, the middle floors of ToA are nowadays too tanky for casual players to do well given the current difficulty, and Carlotta now needs Sequence Nodes or temporary endgame buffs more than ever to be able to clear the game’s hardest content. Her most recent buff is the release of the new 3.0 permanent banner weapons, among which is Phasic Homogenizer, a fantastic DPS Pistol that renders her Signature weapon completely skippable. However, it did not increase her damage ceiling - it only made her more accessible for budgeting (and it doesn’t change the fact that she still needs premium teammates to perform).

In conclusion, Carlotta is nowadays not a recommended pull. There are too many newer, more performant damage dealers who work across all endgames and share similar qualities to her to consider her a worthwhile pull. However, for players who already own her, she remains easily usable in some of the game’s easier content, provided you surround her with the right teammates. It’s still completely true that Carlotta is a consistent and easy-to-pilot character, and those are her main strengths that players who can make use of her will get to enjoy even today.
profile.pros:
• Probably the most consistent DPS in the game. All of her and her teammates’ attacks are ranged in all of her best teams, so she will very rarely (if ever) get interrupted by enemy attacks (so long as you space yourself properly during her Ultimate, but that isn’t hard to do at all);

  • Does not need her Signature weapon to perform in the slightest - Phasic Homogenizer’s existence makes it one of the most skippable Signature weapons in the game.

  • Managed to survive powercreep decently despite being a very old character.
profile.cons:
• Her teammates are either very high-value (Lynae/Mornye) or have not reran in ages (Zhezhi) so it’s unlikely most players have a strong team for her;

  • Low Quickswap compatibility because of major Ultimate self-buffs expiring on Swap;

  • Completely useless in Whimpering Wastes. Zero reason to be used over almost any more recent characters, even in F2P teams compared to Carlotta’s full premium.

profile.rotations:
Rotation & How to Play

Carlotta is one of the easiest characters to pilot in Wuthering Waves. The fundamentals of her playstyle amount to building up her Forte through Intros and Skills, consuming it through her Heavy Attack, and then unleashing the bulk of her damage via her Ultimate sequence. Below are the easiest and most optimal ways to do so.

Echo Timing

Carlotta can cast Sentry Construct’s base form once in her Opener in Quickswap for some extra damage if possible. Otherwise, she will cast the enhanced form at the end of her rotation and Swap Cancel it (either directly in her rotation itself, or optionally by swapping back after her Outro if needed to save time).

Opener (Important)

Before Carlotta can properly begin her rotations, she needs to cast her Skills at the start of the fight. This is to generate 30/120 Substance, as she generates 90 through her Intro and two of her Skills.

  • Skill: Art of Violence

  • Skill: Chromatic Splendor (Swap)

This only needs to be performed once per fight, but since this will send her Skills on a 14s cooldown, it is highly advised to do this immediately before setting up any other character buffs (except maybe Lynae’s Ultimate if you’re using her).

Standard Rotation

Now that Carlotta has 30 Substance to start her rotations with, she can loop the following rotation:

  • Intro

  • Skill: Art of Violence

  • Skill: Chromatic Splendor

  • Basic: Mid-air Attack

  • Heavy: Imminent Oblivion (Cancel animation endlag via Ultimate)

  • Ultimate: Era of New Wave

  • Ultimate: Death Knell (4 times)

  • Ultimate: Fatal Finale

  • Skill: Art of Violence

  • Skill: Chromatic Splendor (Optionally Swap Cancel)

  • Outro

This rotation is performed in order to ensure Carlotta never has to generate any Substance through slow/low-damaging means like her Basic Attacks.

Additional Tips & Tricks

Carlotta’s final Skill before her Outro may be optionally Swap Cancelled if your team’s loop rotation is significantly over Carlotta’s Ultimate cooldown in length. In those cases, her Echo must be cast during another character’s rotation at least a few seconds before Carlotta Intros back in, to ensure she gets the damage from the Echo cast off. If she has the time to spare (will be the case in optimized Zhezhi+Shorekeeper rotations), not Swap Cancelling her final Skill is your best bet to preserve Outro buffs on it before swapping out.

During the team’s Opener rotation, if you have a Swap Cancel window, you can use it for the base cast of Carlotta’s Echo for some extra damage on your first rotation.

If needed, to quickly finish off an enemy without much HP left, it is possible to interrupt all of Carlotta’s Death Knells with a Dash each, in order to fire off her second Ultimate much quicker, although this very rarely (if ever) sees use.

S1+ can give 30 extra Substance on a Skill cast, which can be useful in niche situations (very fast Openers and potentially single 2-Skill loops in Quickswap as well), but generally sticking to the rotation above should work best for most players.

skills.name: Silent Execution
skills.description:
Basic Attack

Perform up to 2 consecutive strikes, dealing Glacio DMG.

Basic Attack - Necessary Measures

With Moldable Crystals, Carlotta's Basic Attack is replaced with Necessary Measures.

Chain up to 3 strikes, dealing Glacio DMG. Each strike of Necessary Measures consumes 1 Moldable Crystal.

Heavy Attack

Deliver a charged attack at the target at the cost of STA, dealing Glacio DMG.

Heavy Attack - Containment Tactics

When Carlotta's Substance is full, her Heavy Attack will be replaced with Containment Tactics: consume all Substance to deal Glacio DMG and reduce the cooldown of Resonance Skill Art of Violence by 6s.

Mid-air Attack

Perform a Plunging Attack at the cost of STA, dealing Glacio DMG. Using Basic Attack shortly after the landing will cast Customary Greetings.

Mid-air Attack - Customary Greetings

Flip over the target and deliver a surprise shot, dealing Glacio DMG.

Dodge Counter

Press Normal Attack shortly after a successful Dodge to deliver a riposte shot, dealing Glacio DMG. This consumes 1 Moldable Crystal.

skills.name: Art of Violence
skills.description:
Deal Glacio DMG and inflict Dispersion on the target. Press Resonance Skill again shortly after to cast Chromatic Splendor.

Dispersion

Targets with Dispersion are immobilized for 1.5s.

Chromatic Splendor

Consume all Moldable Crystals and deal Glacio DMG.

The Resonance Skill enters cooldown after a while if Chromatic Splendor is not cast or Carlotta is switched off the field.

skills.name: Era of New Wave
skills.description:
Deal Glacio DMG to all targets in an area (considered Resonance Skill DMG) and inflict Deconstruction on targets hit, then activate Twilight Tango.

Can be cast in mid-air close to the ground.

Deconstruction

Dealing DMG to targets inflicted with Deconstruction ignores 18% of their DEF.

Twilight Tango

While in Twilight Tango, press Normal Attack or Resonance Liberation to cast Death Knell.

Each Death Knell grants 1 Meta Vector.

With 4 Meta Vectors, press Normal Attack or Resonance Liberation to cast Fatal Finale.

  • All Substance is removed when activating and ending Twilight Tango. Cannot perform Basic Attack Necessary Measures, Heavy Attack Containment Tactics, and Heavy Attack Imminent Oblivion while in Twilight Tango.

Death Knell

Carlotta fires powerful shots with her musket and summons 4 crystal shards to attack the target, dealing Glacio DMG, considered Resonance Skill DMG.

  • Carlotta moves in the direction of the movement input with each shot of Death Knell.

Fatal Finale

Deal Glacio DMG to an area, considered Resonance Skill DMG.

  • Twilight Tango ends after casting Fatal Finale.

skills.name: Lethal Repertoire
skills.description:
Heavy Attack - Imminent Oblivion

  • Carlotta activates Tinted Crystal every 22s.

  • When Substance is full and Tinted Crystal is activated, hold Normal Attack to consume all Substance and cast Heavy Attack Imminent Oblivion, after which Tinted Crystal enters cooldown.

  • Deal Glacio DMG (considered Resonance Skill DMG), and reduce the cooldown of Resonance Skill Art of Violence by 6s.

Final Bow

  • When Substance is full, enter the Final Bow state.

  • Increase the DMG Multiplier of Resonance Liberation Era of New Wave, Resonance Liberation Death Knell, and Resonance Liberation Fatal Finale by 80%. This effect ends when Carlotta is switched off the field during Twilight Tango or when Twilight Tango ends.

Substance

  • Carlotta can hold up to 120 points of Substance.

  • Cannot gain Substance while in Twilight Tango triggered by Resonance Liberation.

  • Restore 30 point of Substance upon casting Intro Skill Wintertime Aria.

  • Restore 10 point of Substance for every 1 Moldable Crystal consumed upon casting Resonance Skill Chromatic Splendor.

  • Restore 10 point of Substance for every 1 Moldable Crystal consumed upon casting Basic Attack Necessary Measures.

  • Consume 1 Moldable Crystal and restore 10 point of Substance upon casting Dodge Counter.

Moldable Crystal

  • Carlotta can hold up to 6 Moldable Crystals.

  • Cannot gain Moldable Crystal while in Twilight Tango triggered by Resonance Liberation.

  • Restore 3 Moldable Crystal upon casting Basic Attack Stage 2.

  • Restore 3 Moldable Crystal upon casting Heavy Attack.

  • Restore 3 Moldable Crystal upon casting Mid-air Attack Customary Greetings.

  • Restore 3 Moldable Crystal upon casting Intro Skill Wintertime Aria.

  • Restore 3 Moldable Crystal upon casting Resonance Skill Art of Violence.

  • Restore 3 Moldable Crystal upon a successful Dodge.

weapons.Comment: The best Carlotta stat-stick that gives her a simple 12% ATK and 48% Skill DMG via its passive as well as a huge CRIT DMG stat and a good Base ATK. Pretty self-explanatory.

An amazing generalist permanently available pistol that can universally improve the wearer's ATK, DMG Bonus and CRIT DMG. Can get close to a lot of character signatures and is overall a must-have for most accounts. Highly recommended on Carlotta instead of her Signature, as it is permanently accessible and barely comes up short of her best in slot.
Simple ATK and CRIT Rate stat-stick for Carlotta, who does not benefit from this weapon's Aero Erosion-focused effects.
Simple ATK and CRIT Rate stat-stick for Carlotta, who barely benefits from this weapon's Basic DMG-increasing effect.
Simple ATK and CRIT DMG stat-stick for Carlotta, who cannot benefit from this weapon's Heavy and Echo DMG-related effects.

Support-focused permanently accessible 5-star weapon. Can provide some ATK% to the next character who Intros in from Carlotta, has a small Energy Regen boost and a nice Base ATK/CRIT Rate, however it's outclassed on her by Phasic Homogenizer quite significantly, and is better relegated to Support options like Lynae who can buff Carlotta with it instead.
Carlotta's best 4-star weapon which gives her a good amount of ATK and Skill DMG when casting Intro. Still not ideal compared to any other 5-star.
This weapon provides some ATK and flat Energy restoration to Carlotta, but it's overall not enough for her to clear endgame content with comfortably anymore. Generally not recommended.

Best fully F2P-accessible option which outclasses all non-listed 4-star Pistol choices, but its passive does require Carlotta to never take any damage from the enemy. However, she is one of the easiest characters to do this with thanks to her really high attack range, so overall this weapon synergizes quite well with her. That being said, weapons other than Phasic Homogenizer and above probably are not enough to clear endgame comfortably, so keep this as a temporary choice.

echoes.Comment: Carlotta's best set bar none, that gives her an unconditional 12% Skill DMG Bonus, 22.5% Glacio DMG Bonus and up to an extra 36% Skill DMG Bonus when casting 2 or more Ultimates (a condition that she easily fulfills). Overall gives a total of 70.5% DMG Bonus at maximum which should speak volumes on how good this set is for Carlotta.
echoes.Echo_1_Comment: The best Main Echo choice for the Frosty Resolve set as it grants 12% Glacio DMG and 12% Skill DMG Bonus when equipped in the main slot. Its active skill also deals a chunk of damage while freezing enemies in place for a short amount of time if fully stacked (which only Carlotta can do). The base cast can also be used during optimized Opener rotations to squeeze a small amount of extra damage.

teams.Comments: Mornye is only best with Lynae on the team.

synergies.Comment: Carlotta's best buffers and second slot partners as she ideally works in hypercarry compositions. Zhezhi and Lynae are easily the best ones as Lynae has a ton of super strong generalist buffs while Zhezhi gives Carlotta a lot of Energy to lower her Energy Regen requirements while also giving the highest DMG Amplification of all her Supports (45% total) and having fast rotation times, enabling consistent 25s team loops. Brant and Cantarella are good alternatives as while they only provide 25% DMG Amplification, they both have solid personal damage and retain reasonable rotation times.

Free-to-play accessible secondary characters for Carlotta teams. While Yangyang does not give any major buffs to Carlotta, her super fast rotation and extra Energy funneling via Outro (reminiscent of Zhezhi) make Carlotta easy to build and rotate with, while she can rely on her third slot partner for extra buffs making the team viable. While Taoqi does have 38% Skill DMG Amplification on her Outro, it does come at the cost of a rather slow and clunky rotation, next to nonexistent personal damage and she does also increase Carlotta's Energy Regen requirements. Overall, Yangyang will be much easier to play but Taoqi can yield higher results if played at her best. Choose based on what category of player you fit in.

These are all of Carlotta's 3rd slot teammate options. Mornye has a special synergy with Lynae since Lynae can apply Tune Rupture/Strain for Mornye to respond to them and provide her full array of buffs, making her the best choice if Lynae is in use. Shorekeeper and Verina are the next best ones as they tend to be some of the best generalist Supports for all ATK and CRIT-scaling DPS due to their super high buffs for short rotation times. Buling still does present herself as a good F2P alternative because Buling trades team-wide ATK buffs for Skill DMG buffs to Carlotta and more personal damage for slightly higher rotation times, which makes her not too far behind Verina, equaling her when optimized at S6.
